sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Interesting! When I tried RIGHT and LEFT from position (22, 22), the player didn't move - stayed at (22, 22). But DOWN moved from (16, 22) to (22, 22), and UP moved from (22, 22) back to (16, 22). This tells me:
1. The grid cells are 6 pixels apart (center-to-center)
2. RIGHT and LEFT from (22, 22) hit walls (blocked cells)
3. The maze has walls that prevent movement in certain directions
Now I understand the movement model better. Let me build a proper grid by exploring from the starting position. The player is currently at (16, 22). Let me go back to the start and map the maze properly.
Actually, let me first figure out the grid structure. The cells seem to be at positions like:
- Row centers: 16, 22, 28, 34, 40, 46, ... (step of 6)
- Col centers: 16, 22, 28, 34, 40, 46, ... (step of 6)
Let me build a grid using these coordinates and then use BFS on the actual maze.

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# Player is at (16, 22). Let me go back to start first
result = action(['LEFT', 'UP', 'LEFT'])  # Go back to start area
seg = current_frame.segmentation
for n in seg['nodes']:
    if n['color'] == 'b':
        boundary = n['boundary']
        rows = [p[0] for p in boundary]
        cols = [p[1] for p in boundary]
        center_r = sum(rows) // len(rows)
        center_c = sum(cols) // len(cols)
        print(f"Player at: ({center_r}, {center_c})")

# Now let me build the grid properly
# Cell centers are at multiples of 6 offset from 16
# Rows: 16, 22, 28, 34, 40, 46, 52, 58
# Cols: 16, 22, 28, 34, 40, 46, 52, 58

# Get all walkable cell centers from segmentation
seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']

cell_centers = {}
for n in nodes:
    if n['color'] in ['W', 'g', 'b', 'N']:
        boundary = n['boundary']
        rows = [p[0] for p in boundary]
        cols = [p[1] for p in boundary]
        center_r = sum(rows) // len(rows)
        center_c = sum(cols) // len(cols)
        # Snap to grid
        grid_r = round((center_r - 16) / 6)
        grid_c = round((center_c - 16) / 6)
        cell_centers[(grid_r, grid_c)] = n['color']

print(f"\nGrid cells found: {len(cell_centers)}")
grid_rows = sorted(set(r for r, c in cell_centers.keys()))
grid_cols = sorted(set(c for r, c in cell_centers.keys()))
print(f"Rows: {grid_rows}, Cols: {grid_cols}")

# Build grid
grid = {}
player_pos = None
goal_pos = None
for (r, c), color in cell_centers.items():
    grid[(r, c)] = color
    if color == 'b':
        player_pos = (r, c)
    elif color == 'N':
        goal_pos = (r, c)

print(f"Player: {player_pos}, Goal: {goal_pos}")
for r in grid_rows:
    row_str = ""
    for c in grid_cols:
        row_str += grid.get((r, c), '.')
    print(f"  Row {r}: {row_str}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
